name: Animal Nutrition & Feed Science

objectives.text: Sort common livestock feeds, such as hay, grain, and pasture grass, by the animals that eat them
Explain why animals need a constant supply of clean, fresh water every day
Distinguish roughages such as hay, pasture, and silage from concentrates such as corn and oats by their appearance, texture, and fiber content
Describe the six major classes of nutrients animals need: water, protein, carbohydrates, fats, vitamins, and minerals
Explain the main job of each nutrient class in an animal's body, such as supplying energy, building muscle, or forming bone
Classify livestock feeds and feeding strategies as suited to ruminant or monogastric animals
Group common feedstuffs as roughages, energy concentrates, protein supplements, or mineral and vitamin supplements
Identify the guaranteed analysis values for crude protein, crude fat, and crude fiber on a commercial feed tag
Assign a body condition score to a livestock animal and recommend whether its feeding level should increase, decrease, or stay the same
Calculate the daily feed intake an animal needs based on its body weight and a given feeding rate
Calculate feed conversion and cost of gain from supervised agricultural experience records of feed fed and weight gained
Analyze the role of each essential nutrient, including specific vitamins and macro and trace minerals, in animal growth and performance
Differentiate the nutrient requirements of animals for maintenance, growth, gestation, lactation, and work across species and production systems
Interpret the components of a feed label and apply its feeding directions to feed a project animal
Convert feedstuff nutrient values between an as-fed basis and a dry matter basis
Explain how feed processing methods such as grinding, rolling, pelleting, and ensiling affect palatability and nutrient digestibility
Balance a ration with the Pearson square or a spreadsheet so it meets an animal's protein and energy requirements for its stage of production
Compare feeds using energy measures such as total digestible nutrients and net energy
Evaluate forage quality from a hay or silage test report using values such as crude protein, ADF, NDF, and relative feed value
Evaluate the adequacy of an existing ration using feedstuff analysis, animal requirements, and performance data
Select feedstuffs for a ration based on cost per unit of nutrient, digestive system, nutritional needs, and local availability
Recommend whether to use feed additives and growth promotants based on scientific evidence, Veterinary Feed Directive rules, production goals, and industry standards
Design a complete feeding program for a livestock enterprise that balances ration cost, nutrient requirements, and feed availability across production stages

changes: I kept all six existing objectives, rewording two of them lightly. I filled gaps across the grade span: water, roughages versus concentrates, nutrient functions, feedstuff groups, reading feed tags, body condition scoring, feed conversion and cost of gain from SAE records, as-fed versus dry matter conversion, feed processing, energy measures, forage testing, ration evaluation, feedstuff selection, and feed additives with the VFD. The Pearson square ration objective gained a spreadsheet option. I attached AFNR Animal Systems standards only to grade 9 to 12 objectives that teach them. I left out the FPP human-nutrition standards and digestive anatomy, disease, and welfare content because those belong to other sub-topics.
